title: OS and utilities worksheet
subject: Computing
source: Seeded from computing/y9 lesson 9 (OS and utilities worksheet (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 9: Operating systems and utility software. To understand the functions of an operating system and why utility software is needed

questions.q: Name three functions of an operating system.
questions.a: For example: memory management, file management, user interface.
questions.model: Teacher links each function to something pupils did today: logging in (security), opening Teams (memory and CPU), saving (file management).

questions.q: Why might a school run backups every night?
questions.a: So work can be recovered if a device fails or files are deleted.

questions.q: Why is defragmentation not used on SSDs?
questions.a: SSDs have no moving parts, so access is fast anyway, and it wears the drive.

questions.q: Core: Explain how an operating system lets you use Teams, a browser and a document at once, in the portal response box. Start: 'The operating system...'
questions.a: The operating system shares CPU time between the programs in quick turns and gives each its own memory space; if RAM fills, it uses virtual memory.
questions.model: Teacher writes the first sentence: 'The operating system gives each program a turn on the CPU...'

questions.q: Extend: Compare a GUI and a command-line interface: one advantage of each.
questions.a: GUI: easy for beginners; command line: fast and powerful for experts, uses fewer resources.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why antivirus software must be updated regularly.
questions.a: New malware appears all the time; updates add new signatures so it can be recognised.

questions.q: Which is NOT a job of an operating system? A) memory management B) writing essays C) file management
Big question: how does one processor run three programs at once?
questions.a: The OS shares CPU time between them in very quick turns (multitasking).
